Mission 02 · Word detective

What job does a word do?

5 min
NOUN

A person, place, thing or idea

explorer · ocean · adventure

VERB

An action or state

explore · sail · swim

ADJECTIVE

Describes a noun

brave · dangerous · spectacular

ADVERB

Often describes how an action happens

slowly · carefully · suddenly

Look at the sentence: The brave sailor sailed carefully. sailor = noun · brave = adjective · sailed = verb · carefully = adverb.

Sort the words

Mission 03 · Student's Book · Unit 2 Adventure

Read: Exploration

6 min

Open Student's Book, page 23, Exercise 1. Read the original text and answer the questions below.

exploration

Yesterday, sixteen-year-old Hector Turner began his attempt to become the youngest Briton to complete a 242 km ‘ultra-marathon’ across the Sahara Desert. On the same day, Geordie Stewart, a twenty-year-old university student, set off for Everest. He wanted to be the youngest Briton to achieve the ‘Seven Summits’ challenge – climbing the highest mountain on each continent. Last year, Mike Perham circumnavigated the world alone by boat at the age of seventeen.

Why do today’s teenagers feel this need for exploration and adventure? Why do they want to have wild experiences? Mike Perham has a theory: ‘Kids dream more than adults.’

Check your understanding

Find the word forms in the text

Find and say aloud:

  • one noun: exploration
  • one verb: explore (think of the word family)
  • one adjective: youngest
  • one noun that names an activity: adventure

Grammar review · Student's Book p. 22

Past Simple or Past Continuous?

4 min
Past Continuous

was / were + verb-ing

An action in progress in the past.

He was sailing.
Past Simple

past form of the verb

A completed or shorter action.

He saw a shark.
Compare: He was sailing when he saw a shark. The longer action was in progress; the shorter action happened during it.

Quick check

Then complete Student's Book, page 22, Exercise 3 with your teacher: the full text about Harry and the shark.

Mission 06 · Speak and create

Tell your ocean adventure

7 min

Imagine you were on a boat. Something surprising happened. Plan a short story and tell it to your teacher.

Use adventure chunks

a remote place · a spectacular view · a brave person · a thrilling experience · That's so impressive!

Use both past tenses

I was sailing when…

While I was looking at the sea…

Suddenly, I saw…

Plan your story

Try to include 3 nouns, 2 verbs, 2 adjectives, one Past Continuous sentence and one Past Simple sentence.

Great! Tell your story aloud. Your teacher can give feedback on vocabulary, word forms and past tenses.
